assessments.headline: A few things are worth improving

result.headline: A few things are worth improving

factors.label: Blood pressure
factors.tip: Recheck on separate days and discuss it with a doctor, especially with other risk factors.

factors.label: Total cholesterol
factors.tip: Review diet and activity, and discuss the full lipid profile with a doctor.

factors.label: Fasting blood sugar
factors.detail: High blood sugar quietly damages blood vessels.
factors.tip: A fasting glucose or HbA1c test is quick and inexpensive.

factors.label: Body mass index
factors.tip: A 5 to 10 percent weight loss lowers blood pressure and sugar.

factors.label: Smoking
factors.detail: Quitting has already reduced your risk.
factors.tip: Stay smoke-free and avoid second-hand smoke.

factors.label: Physical activity
factors.detail: Well below the 150 minutes a week guideline.
factors.tip: Start with 10 minute brisk walks and build up.

result.context: Age and sex also shape risk but cannot be changed. This check counts well-known risk factors and is not a prediction of whether you have heart disease.
next_steps: Ask for a blood pressure, lipid profile, and blood sugar check at your next doctor visit.
If you ever get chest pain or pressure, breathlessness on mild effort, or fainting, use the symptom check or see a doctor.
For a formal 10-year risk estimate, ask your doctor to use a validated population calculator.

model.headline: Worth getting checked
model.summary: Your answers sit in the middle: some patients with similar answers had significant blockage and many did not.
model.action: Book a doctor visit in the next few weeks and ask whether an ECG or a stress test makes sense.
